appsScript.title: Google Apps Script setup
appsScript.desc: Sync keeps everything in a Google Sheet you own. Set the backend up once, then paste its URL and token into Cloud sync above.
appsScript.downloadHint: Both files belong in the same Apps Script project.
appsScript.step1Body: Open a new spreadsheet. Every synced row — projects, pages, blocks, glossary, settings, usage stats and, if you switch it on, API keys — is written there.
appsScript.step2Body: Extensions → Apps Script. Delete any placeholder code and paste Code.gs in. Then paste appsscript.json over the manifest (View → Show manifest file).
appsScript.step3Body: Project Settings → Script Properties → add TOKEN = a long random string of 32 or more characters. It travels with every request and is never written into the file or the sheet.
appsScript.step4Body: Deploy → New deployment → Type: Web app → Execute as: Me → Who has access: Anyone → Authorize (the spreadsheet scope only). Copy the /exec URL it shows.
appsScript.step5Body: Paste that /exec URL into Apps Script URL and type the same token into Access token, both in Cloud sync above.
appsScript.step6Body: Press Test connection — the backend creates any missing sheets on its first ping — then press Sync now.
appsScript.updateBody: Deploy → Manage deployments → Edit → Version: New version → Deploy. Re-pasting the code without bumping the version leaves this app talking to the old file.
appsScript.ownNote: The spreadsheet, the script and the token are all yours. This app only ever reads and writes the sheets it was pointed at.

export.title: Export document
export.includeOriginal: Keep the source text next to the translation
export.includeImages: Embed page artwork behind the text
export.adjustLayout: Adjust layout when a translation grows
export.adjustLayoutDesc: Off, by default: every block stays where the PDF put it, which is what an image export promises. On: a block that will not fit even at its smallest readable size is pushed down over the ones below, exactly as the HTML and print exports do — and any block the page edge stops is reported after the export.
export.pdfExplainer: The PDF keeps real vector text — selectable and searchable — and is produced through the browser’s print dialog using the bundled Myanmar fonts. Choose Raster PDF instead if you need a pixel-exact copy.
export.rasterExplainer: The raster PDF is pixel-exact: every page is an image, so no print dialog is used and there is no text layer — the text cannot be selected or searched, and the file is larger.
export.missingFontsBody: The browser does not have these families. Each one would be replaced with:
export.issueLayoutBody: This browser gave the export no way to measure text, so blocks were re-flowed from an estimated character width. A block may sit a line further down than it needed to — nothing is missing.
export.issueClippedBody: The page box is fixed, so they were parked at the bottom edge and overlap the block above. Nothing is missing.
